Issue #108: Fix duplicate results being returned from similarity matching

Description:
## Problem

The similarity matching system is returning duplicate results instead of unique matches. This is a reproducible bug where the same contributor recommendations appear multiple times.

## Context

Referenced from: https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-config/issues/16#issuecomment-3121778678

The issue shows that when querying for suitable contributors, the system consistently returns 2 identical results instead of a single result or different candidates.

## Expected Behavior

The similarity matching should return unique results without duplicates.

## Suspected Cause

The bug likely stems from:
- Multiple event listeners being attached
- The same event being invoked multiple times
- Duplicate vector similarity calculations

## Investigation Needed

- Check if there are multiple event handlers processing the same request
- Verify vector similarity calculation logic for deduplication
- Review the response formatting to ensure unique results only

Issue #45: Pull Precheck Description: We have waves of contributors that open pulls sometimes keeping our review team busy. We can save valuable man hours by having the bot preemptively check if the pull achieves the specification. ### Pull Flow 1. Assuming that the contributor follows directions, the pull must be initially opened up as a draft. 2. When it is ready for review, they should turn it into a finalized pull request. 3. The bot should consume the issue specification and then the pull diff into its context. 4. The bot should return actionable feedback for what is missing from the specification. It should leave the review state as requested changes. It should also convert the pull back into a draft. However if it passes, it should leave as just "commented" (not approval). 5. If a collaborator (reviewer on the team) converts the pull back from a draft into a finalized pull, then the bot should back off and stop intervening. Basically the inspection should only occur on pull.created and when it's converted from draft to finalized by the pull author. Bonus but maybe can be handled in other tasks: 1. Ensure CI is passing. I didn't include this here because sometimes there are problems out of the control of the pull author. 2. Limits: some novice contributors might abuse the code review feature and burn out credits by continuously requesting reviews every time they make a tiny change that doesn't achieve the specification. We have seen folks do hundreds of commits for tasks that required a small amount of lines of code. We can limit the reviews to one per day for the LLM. However it isn't clear to me how we can automatically have it check again the next day if they request a review. Maybe that can be handled by some later task. We should use Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Issue #997: Integrate Liquity V1 Stability Pool for LUSD Collateral Yield

Description:

## Problem
Plain LUSD collateral earns 0% yield. Integrate Stability Pool for ~6.28% APR ([Dune data](https://dune.com/liquity/liquity-v1)) to fund governance token buybacks, without disrupting liquidity.

## Solution
Add `StabilityPoolFacet` via diamond proxy. Auto-deposit LUSD to pool on mint; withdraw principal on redeem. Harvest ETH/LQTY yields during redeems for buybacks/compounding (protocol-owned only). Piggyback ops on user txs for gas efficiency.

## Alternatives Considered
- AAVE (~3.24% yield, more complex).
- Leverage/LPs (higher risk).
- V2 migration (future option for multi-collateral).

## Implementation Spec
### ~~Prerequisites~~
- ~~Audit facet (~$10-20K budget).~~
- ~~Integrate `IStabilityPool.sol` (address: 0x66017D22b0f8556afDd19e1e5b5f1cbD89a6C337).~~
- ~~Add 1inch/Uniswap for swaps.~~
- ~~New storage: `totalPrincipalInPool` (uint256), `protocolTreasury` (address).~~

### Facet Functions
- `depositToPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `provideToSP(amount, address(0))`.
- `withdrawFromPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `withdrawFromSP(amount)`.
- `harvestRewards()`: Claim rewards, swap (e.g., 50% to LUSD for compounding, 50% to governance token for buybacks).

### Flows
- **Mint**: Transfer LUSD → Deposit to pool → Mint uUSD → Update `totalPrincipalInPool += amount`.
- **Redeem**: Burn uUSD → Calc principal → Withdraw/transfer principal → Harvest if rewards > threshold (route to treasury) → Update `totalPrincipalInPool -= amount`.

### Over-Collateralization
Value pool as LUSD equivalent (Chainlink oracles for ETH/LQTY). Redemptions: principal only.

### Monitoring/Automation
- Chainlink/Gelato for optional harvests. It would be nice to sell the ETH/LQTY for LUSD and boost holdings as soon as it is rewarded by the stability pool.
- Dune alerts for APR/supply.

## Testing
- Unit: Deposit/withdraw/harvest (Foundry).
- Integration: Mainnet fork; simulate liquidations.
- Edges: Low liquidity, volatility, mass redeems. Gas: <200K extra per tx.

## Deployment
1. Deploy facet.
2. `diamondCut` via multisig.
3. Verify on Etherscan.
4. Phased: Opt-in for new deposits.

## ~~Risks/Mitigations~~
- ~~Yield variability: Fallback to plain LUSD if APR <3%.~~
- ~~Supply crunch: Auto-withdraw if < $10M.~~
- ~~Security: Audit for reentrancy.~~

Issue #385: GitHub Decoupling

Description:
As we start market research on repurposing our tech for other use cases, I realized that if we rely on GitHub for this to work, it limits us to servicing developers. 

I propose building an integration with any popular task management software like asana or even Google Sheets possibly (to save you headache, find one with good APIs and docs) 

This will force you to begin decoupling the architecture from the GitHub dependency. Then this plugin will be portable to other project management software. 

It is not clear to me if our kernel supports this, but assuming that it does, then I imagine these changes can be applied on this plugin in less than a week.

I have mixed feelings on Google Sheets because it will take time to figure out how to make the UX make sense. For example you need to figure how to make a "formula" that can render a button or checkbox, that represents the project is closed as complete. 

I suppose as another project we also need to associate one humans identity across several platforms.

Issue #36: Preview deployments for Workers

Description:
This is not a specific plugin but a nice-to-have features for plugin Workers.

Currently when developing it's quite easy to switch to a different Action branch for testing a new feature, by specifying the `@branch` within the configuration.

However, workers do not benefit from this and always have to be deployed from the main branch to be tested. This makes development more tedious than it has to be, even worse when testing other people pull-requests.

What would be nice is to get a preview URL base on the latest commit of the branch the user is working on.

It would also be important to cleanup the preview deployments as they would pollute Cloudflare heavily.

A naming pattern could be:
`<plugin-name>.<username>.<branch>.<hash>` to find them easily and know what they refer to. We could also have the deployed url displayed in the Action results to be found easily, and without the need to access Github token because we do not publish in the pull-request thread.

This probably can be implemented as an Action, which we could also put inside the `plugin-template` so new plugins can benefit from this right away.

Issue #54: Merge configurations by unique IDs

Description:
We should look into a more robust configuration merge.

Quote from discussion:

I know there isn't a concept of merging configurations together on GitHub Actions. 

This doesn't address the key point I am making. The cause we are discussing is a collision with dependency IDs. And whether there are real-world scenarios where configurations might lead to duplicate dependencies. 

From my experience creating GitHub Actions CI scripts, I haven't encountered situations where adding redundant dependencies was necessary. This makes the theoretical merging logic problem irrelevant to our practical implementation. 

We should focus on the actual conditions under which our configurations operate, rather than hypothetical scenarios that don't align with real-world use cases.

Basically I'm saying to drop support for using the same dependency more than one, particularly when associated with the same webhook event. See [this comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquibot-kernel/pull/47#issuecomment-2154146051) for a suggestion on how to handle that.

Issue #76: Automatically set a `Time: ` label

Description:
I ran an experiment of automatically generating subtasks for https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/421

I told Claude to provide a time estimate based on the issue specification and divide it by 15. So a 15-hour task yields 1 hour. 

Then take a look at the existing `Time: ` labels of the repository and label with the best fitting one.

---

Due to some problems with Claude this week (horrible at following instructions, rumored that they are quantizing the model to save on costs this last week) I switched over to Grok. Grok code seemed to not need the time offset. 

---

Make a plug-in that listens to issue created or specification edited and automatically sets a time label based on similar instructions.

---

I do prefer using Claude because it's included with my Claude Code 20x Max plan. 

Try getting it to work with `claude -p "my prompt here`"! I added a couple extra hours here cause of prompting and testing. I imagine if it only has to worry about a single issue, it should be better at following instructions. 


Another remark is that I specifically tried to remove bias by telling it to ignore the original time estimate listed. Just provide a new estimate.

Make the offset configurable, because I imagine that as the models improve, this offset will change.

Issue #261: Callbacks - event handlers and hybrid plugins

Description:
I want to improve the experience of setting up event handlers and hybrid plugins.
I imagine something like this

```js
.on("issue_comment.created", "action", handler1)
.on("issue.closed", "worker", handler2)
```

The SDK would handle calling the Action or run it normally as a Worker and in case you're running it locally it would execute Action handlers locally too. 
Sometimes the reason why we need to call it as an Action is because some libraries are not supported by CF Workers so it'd be also good to have an option to run it as an Action even if you're running it locally.
Current hybrid plugins use `ACTION_REF` to know which Action to call but it'd be great if we could somehow get it automatically but I realize that may be not feasible.

At this point I would also consider merging `createActionsPlugin` and `createPlugin` for seamless experience.

I also realized that maybe we don't need kernel credentials to trigger Action from the Worker but only a fine-grained Github token that would only have access to the repo. Because we don't change the payload but only forward it to the Action, we don't need to generate a new signature and we can keep the original.

Issue #6: WalletConnect/Reown Integration – Handoff

Description:
# WalletConnect/Reown Integration – Handoff

Objective
- Implement wallet connection UX using WalletConnect/Reown only (no Coinbase SDK, no extra connector stacks) on top of wagmi v2 + viem v2; ensure parity across mainnet and local anvil (31337) modes.

Context
- Repo: `stake.ubq.fi` (branch `pr-1`)
- Stack: React 19, wagmi 2.x, viem 2.x, TanStack Query 5
- Modes: `dev` (public RPC), `local-node` (anvil on 31337), `prod`

Deliverables
- Integrate Reown (WalletConnect) as the sole wallet provider:
  - Use `@reown/appkit` (+ minimal controllers if needed) with wagmi v2 + viem v2.
  - Read `VITE_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID` from env; if missing, hide WalletConnect UI and show a simple disabled state with guidance.
  - If Reown offers injected/browser support via the same stack, enable it through Reown only (do not add separate injected connectors).
- A `ConnectWalletButton` component with states (disconnected, connecting, connected) and chain awareness, powered by Reown.
- Auto-chain handling:
  - `local-node` mode: support 31337 and do not attempt chain ID suffixing on RPC URLs.
  - dev/prod: support mainnet; prevent auto-switching without user consent.
- Persist connection state (wagmi default).

Acceptance Criteria
- In `dev` mode with Reown configured, `Connect` → shows account and chain; disconnect works.
- In `local-node` mode with anvil running, able to connect and read chain `31337`.
- Only Reown/WalletConnect UI is present; Coinbase and other stacks are not included.
- No blocking console errors; network calls respect `src/constants/config.ts` RPC behavior.

Constraints & Guidance
- Keep bundle size in mind; lazy load Reown UI if possible.
- Avoid adding large UI kits; implement a small, styled button consistent with existing CSS.
- Do not hardcode secrets; rely on `VITE_*` env vars.

Suggested Steps
1) Add Reown packages: `@reown/appkit` (and controllers if needed) and WalletConnect provider as required by Reown docs.
2) Create `src/wallet/config.ts` to centralize wagmi + viem + Reown configuration and chains.
3) Implement `ConnectWalletButton` under `src/components/connect-wallet.tsx` using Reown hooks/APIs.
4) Wire into `src/App.tsx` top bar or dashboard header.
5) Manually test dev and local-node modes.

Validation
- Commands:
  - Dev: `bun run dev` with `VITE_WALLETCONNECT_PROJECT_ID` set → connect via Reown.
  - Local: run anvil + `bun run local` → connect on 31337 via Reown.

Out of Scope
- Full transaction flow QA (approve/stake/claim); addressed separately.

Issue #43: premade configs that are hands-off for partners

Description:
## Premade Configurations vs. Default Plugin Manifests

We aim to streamline the experience for pilot partners by providing **premade configurations**. This approach reduces the need for partners to manually configure plugins. In addition, we provide two alternative ways to modify configurations:

1. Utilize [this feature request](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugins-wishlist/issues/65).
2. Contact customer support for manual adjustments.

### Default Plugin Behavior

1. When a plugin uses `defaults` that are **not** sourced from a **premade config**, it retrieves its configuration from the plugin's `manifest.json` in its respective repository.
2. These defaults originate from `pluginInputs.ts` and are used across multiple infrastructure components, including:
   - This UI
   - Natural language configuration edits
   - Plugin schema and input validation (kernel-side)
   - Other relevant subsystems

#### Opinionated Defaults

There is a general concern about **opinionated defaults**. Instead of enforcing such defaults, we should **only share premade configs with partners**, eliminating the need for them to define their own configurations.

Reference: [Discussion on opinionated defaults](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/151#discussion_r1991092437)

### Configuration Modes

Currently, there are three configuration modes:

- **Minimal**
- **Full Defaults**
- **Custom**

These modes, up to this point, have not been enforced to be unopinionated. Some configurations are highly opinionated and may not align with the principle of **non-opinionated defaults**.

---

## Proposed Solutions

### 1. Establish a Collection of Premade Configurations
- Define a structured set of **premade configs**.
- Ensure each premade config abstracts its functionality at a high level.
- Reduce the cognitive load on partners.

### 2. YAML-Based Template Structure
To further simplify configuration management, I suggest we use a **YAML template** with the following structure:

```yaml
metadata:
  name: "UbiquityOS Standard Config"
  description: "The fully-enabled and battle-tested configuration which we use across all organizations at Ubiquity."
  version: "1.0"

plugins: ...
```

This template includes:
- **Metadata**: Describes the premade configuration.
- **Plugins**: Lists installed plugins with relevant settings.

This abstraction ensures partners **"don’t have to think about it."**

---

## Handling Plugin Expansion

### Default Non-Expanded Behavior
@gentlementlegen [suggests](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/issues/40#issuecomment-2670919061) that plugins should be installed in a **non-expanded state**. This means:

- **Infra fetches only the non-opinionated defaults** when retrieving the plugin’s manifest.
- **If plugin details are expanded**, infra should fetch its specific config **before** relying on the manifest.

### Supporting Only Premade Configs
If we only allow **premade configs** and restrict editing to **already installed plugins**, then:

- Each `premade` configuration will be expanded by default.
- This ensures we avoid relying on **non-opinionated defaults**, which may not align with intended user experiences.

---

## Conclusion

- **Premade configurations** should be the standard approach.
- A **YAML-based template** simplifies configuration abstraction.
- **Non-expanded installations** should default to non-opinionated configurations.
- **Expanded plugin configurations** should fetch predefined configurations before falling back to defaults.

By enforcing these principles, we create a **streamlined, user-friendly**, and **low-maintenance** approach to plugin configuration management.

Issue #263: Model Context Protocol Standard vs Manifests Description: We reinvented the wheel, probably poorly, with our manifests and tool calling via LLMs. We can turn our kernel into a [MCP Client](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/quickstart/client) and the plugins into [MCP Servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/quickstart/server). I was installing a bunch of MCPs for my Cline extension to use and was looking at some source code of an MCP: https://github.com/ferrislucas/iterm-mcp/blob/961882be693b82e258408f24ca1f40ee0a96e033/src/index.ts#L25-L72 Looks familiar. We should adopt the MCP standard because 1. surely Anthropic did a better job designing the architecture 2. interoperability with [all the MCP tools](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers). There's a huge community already. ### Remarks To be honest it isn't clear to me if we must make all of our plugins into MCP servers, or if we just make our kernel into an MCP server. I think there could be some real innovation here to support making Actions/Workers easily into hosted MCP servers with exposed endpoints. This means combining our plugin template with their MCP template. ### Related - https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk?tab=readme-ov-file#low-level-server could be merged with our plugin template. This "low level server" looks awfully familiar to a Cloudflare Worker. Issue #14: UbiquityOS Sprint Management Dashboard

Description:
This is a stub task.

We should make a simple sign up experience meant to convert paying customers, engineering managers specifically.

My vision is to post on places like [hackernews](https://news.ycombinator.com) twitter etc and do a quick writeup on how AI team managers are here, highlighting benefits X, Y, Z...

Then bring them to some marketing/landing page with a sign in with GitHub button. At this time our system can scrape their GitHub organization, generate vector embeddings, and start planning their upcoming sprint.

The user logs into a simplified version of the dashboard that basically shows

1. a calendar view of their real team members and what tasks they should be assigned to (we will need to define priority levels somehow[^1], normally a manager labels each priority level on the task individually.) and we can automatically estimate the time of each task by reading their specifications.
2. Quantitative metrics of how much value the system provides to their team i.e. saves X amount of time assigning tasks (assuming it takes 5 minutes to assign each task from the backlog to the right person etc) and saves Y amount of dollars in a typical engineering manager salary etc. The numbers should be a lot more impressive with larger backlogs (perhaps we can support importing tasks from other platforms like asana etc)

### General Steps

1. Backend
2. Landing Page/Conversion Funnel UI/UX Design
3. Implementation

[^1]: a tinder like view with swiping left (low) right (high) up (urgent) to quickly set priority levels on tasks could be interesting to bootstrap the system's data. But otherwise we can ask the AI to think of what is most likely to drive revenue (business priority) tasks, and we can provide examples like internal developer tooling may be lower priority than fixing breaking bugs.

Issue #270: Review Incentives: Deleted Files

Description:
Count the amount of removed lines for deleted files and subtract from the total lines changed count. 

The reason for this is because when reviewing it takes little/no cognitive overhead on the files view to skim over "file deleted" 

---

> Seems arbitrary and would eventually fail in some cases. It is complex to evaluate line changes because renaming a function for example could involve changing all the import across files and you would end with a +20 -20 for one rename.

This would yield $0.40 which isn't bad. 

The problem is that not every line changed takes the same cognitive overhead to process. 

Obviously most of the 17k removed was cypress code which can be easily reviewed just by reading "file deleted"

Perhaps we can reduce credit based on the deleted files removed line count. 

This will also solve for renames in case git doesn't catch it!

Issue #410: One Review Incentive Per Pull

Description:
The review incentive is broken when paying out per issue when a pull request addresses multiple issues.

## Requirements

- Review rewards must be paid per pull request, not per issue
- Generate unique permits using pull request ID (similar to current issue ID handling) instead of separate nonce system
- Calculate review reward amount using weighted average of priorities and time estimates from linked issues:
  - Formula: `(Priority₁ × Time₁) + (Priority₂ × Time₂) + ...` divided by total time
  - Handle edge cases (e.g., division by zero)
  - Cap maximum reward at highest task reward among linked issues
- Post review rewards exclusively in pull requests (not in issues)
- Maintain issue rewards (for assignees) in original issues
- Use batch claim functionality to manage separate reward permits
- Convert time estimates to consistent units (hours) for calculation:
  - Example conversions:
    - < 15 minutes = 0.25 hours
    - < 1 hour = 1 hour
    - < 4 hours = 4 hours
    - < 1 day = 24 hours
    - < 1 week = 168 hours

## Implementation Notes

- Repository configuration must be inherited for consistent behavior
- Priority levels and time estimates must be included in reward calculation metadata
- Weighted average should emphasize where developers spend actual effort
- Separate issue rewards (for assignees) and PR rewards (for reviewers)
- Maximum one review reward per pull request

Only support settlements using UUSD. 2. Allow the user to configure what asset they want to be paid in, it should be saved in localStorage. 3. The cowswap quote can appear in place of the reward amount. For example, by default, loading the app for `100 UUSD` permit would show that. However there are clearly some contributors that take more resources than they add. The system should restrict them from their ability to participate. We need a means to keep track of when the user is disqualified, and store a negative XP that corresponds with the wasted effort. The simplest would be to store the task amount as a negative, but ideally we should actually calculate the sum total of the rewards that should have been paid out. When the user completes tasks successfully, we save their permit details in the database which can be used to calculate their positive XP. In the config of this plugin, we should be able to set minimum XP to start based on priority levels and/or time levels. Then we can do something like: ``` p0: -2000 p1: -1000 p2: 0 p3: 1000 p4: 2000 p5: 3000 ``` We also should check the account age or activity so that we can't easily be Sybil'd. Issue #111: Nomic Embeddings Model for +10% Accuracy

Description:
The vector embedding model that we use is slightly outdated. I did some research to see what has higher accuracy, and I found one with 10% increased accuracy. We should make use of it as well as our old model.

## Leaderboard

Model | Top-5 Retrieval Accuracy (%) | Notes
-- | -- | --
Nomic Embed v1.5 | ~86.2% | Highest overall retrieval accuracy in semantic search benchmarks, especially strong on short & direct queries. Open source and highly accurate.
Voyage-3-large | ~75-77% | Best model from Voyage AI, state-of-the-art in industry, notably outperforms OpenAI text-embedding-3-large by ~9.7%. Strong on domain-specific tasks.

## Tradeoff

> When you submit a GitHub comment that exceeds the token capacity of the embedding model, typically:
> - The model will truncate the input at its token limit (e.g., 8,192 tokens for Nomic or 32,000 tokens for Voyage).
> - This means any text beyond the max token limit is ignored, which can lead to loss of context and reduced embedding quality if important content is cut off.

## Solution

> 2. Similarity Functions
> - Key Point: Embeddings from different models generally cannot be directly compared using the same similarity function (e.g., cosine or dot product) unless their vector spaces are aligned.
> - Each model produces numerical vectors in its own latent space, meaning the scale, direction, and semantic meaning may differ dramatically.
> - Comparing Nomic vectors against Voyage vectors directly will yield misleading results.
>
> What To Do:
> - In practice, keep embeddings from each model in separate indices or collections.
> - For each query or search, use the correct index according to the embedding model used: maintain “Nomic space” and “Voyage space” separately.

## Remarks

GitHub comment limit is 65,536 characters ≈ 16,384 tokens (rough estimate.) This means that especially comments with metadata unlikely will be able to rely on Nomic (8,192 max tokens)

## Research

https://www.perplexity.ai/search/best-vector-embeddings-model-CSpgO23jTBW5AHrh30a0cA

Issue #196: Automating Call To Action Delivery (Repo XP Report)

Description:
We envision that on our upcoming landing page for the XP product, we need to have a call to action that will convince users to pay for the product. 

The idea is to have them input a repository URL and then we can send them an XP report of the last month for their team. Ideally this would be in the form of a link to the dashboard so they can see everything. 

I imagine that we can leverage the tech from https://github.com/0x4007/travel-stipend/ to trigger a run using text-conversation-rewards https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards/actions/workflows/compute.yml @gentlementlegen please add any necessary details like what branch its on and how to make this all work together. 

### Details on running `text-conversation-rewards` action

- we need to run this securely either through the kernel or calling directly by providing the proper signature
- there should be a way to know if that was previously run on this repo to avoid running it multiple times
- we can ignore private repositories
- at the end of the run, we can send the results via email to the user
- XP is based on priority / rewards combination, we need a way to define what the labels would have been, theoretically

### Safety

We must only allow this to work once per organization. This is so they can only get this free report one time. In theory this can be circumvented if they transfer repos to new orgs but that seems like a lot of headache and unlikely for established orgs to do.

We can make a cron job that runs every day that goes through every plugin on @ubiquity-os-marketplace and if there are 10 consecutive failures, we should get notified.

It might be easiest to post a comment somewhere tagging me and @gentlementlegen to start

---

It seems like we can filter for what was manually dispatched by our two apps.

---

This doesn't need to be configurable. We just want to make it as simple as possible.

[Keyrxng at 2025-12-02T19:25:05Z]:
I'll start this.

1. I can have it create an issue in the target repo or within `.ubiquity-os` and list all failures.

2. Should I collect failure reasons or just the amount of consecutive failures and notify if 10 or more?

[0x4007 at 2025-12-04T07:02:47Z]:
In target repo seems like a good idea @Keyrxng 

I'm not sure but the main point is that we know that it's down and we need to debug. I suppose it would be most convenient to show the error log in the issue directly. 

The more relevant info the better because we can have copilot push a fix right from the issue ui if there is sufficient context. 

Note: because these are hotfixes I don't think we would price them in practice.

@gentlementlegen @whilefoo could you guys help with the review

PR: https://github.com/ubiquity-os/.github/pull/18

Highlights:
- Daily cron + manual trigger monitor workflow
- Scans `ubiquity-os-marketplace` plugin repos for consecutive `workflow_dispatch` failures
- Raises/updates alert issue when failures hit threshold (default 10)
- Includes failure run links + context in alert body
- Unit-tested failure counting and issue body generation

Issue #41: Lower requested permissions on user registration Description: When a new user registers to the website and logs in via GitHub, sensitive rights are requested by the app, which is `read / write` on all `public / private` repositories. This seems to be excessive and worrisome for newcomers as they would wonder why we need to write on their private repos. Ideally, we should just request for read permission on public repos. I do not know myself the reason of the request of such elevated rights, so it would be worth investigating. If elevated rights are indeed needed for core members or insiders of the organization, these rights should be requested specifically for these members not for every new user registering. Issue #22: Predefined configs

Description:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-plugin-installer/pull/13

Right now partner is able to setup bot config individually per plugin.

We should offer predefined configs so that instead of customizing each plugin individually partner could simply select a predefined config.

Simply put partner should be able to:
1. Setup each plugin individually (already implemented)
2. Create a new config from a predefined config template in one click

For the start I think we should support 2 config templates:
1. Config with all plugins from https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace and all default values
2. Minimal:
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing
  - https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards

Notice: the UI should support multiple predefined configs.

Issue #27: Generate manifest metadata from code/package.json (commands, listeners, skipBotEvents, name, description) Description: ## Summary `manifest.json` generation is still partial. We should extend generation so plugin metadata is derived from code (and package metadata) instead of handwritten JSON where possible. Related: ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel#320 ## Current state In `action-deploy-plugin`, we currently auto-generate: - `configuration` (from `pluginSettingsSchema`) And in deploy workflows we already auto-update: - `homepage_url` - `short_name` (already handled by existing automation in current plugin release flows; this issue should not regress that behavior) Still commonly handwritten today: - `name` - `description` - `commands` - `ubiquity:listeners` - `skipBotEvents` (needs a canonical source) This causes drift between code/package metadata and manifest. ## Goal Make `manifest.json` generation code-first for: - `commands` - `ubiquity:listeners` - `skipBotEvents` (from an explicit source) And package-first for: - `name` (from `package.json`) - `description` (from `package.json`) while preserving current automation for: - `homepage_url` - `short_name` ## Proposal ### 1) Generate `commands` from code - Add support in `action-deploy-plugin` to read command metadata from a typed source (for example, exported command schema metadata or a dedicated manifest-meta export). - Emit `manifest.commands` from that source during build. ### 2) Generate `ubiquity:listeners` from code - Add support to derive listeners from a typed source (for example, `SupportedEvents` export or explicit listeners export). - Emit `manifest["ubiquity:listeners"]` during build. ### 3) Add canonical source for `skipBotEvents` - Introduce one explicit code location for this flag (for example, `manifestMeta.skipBotEvents` export). - During generation, set `manifest.skipBotEvents` from that source. - Avoid implicit defaults hidden across multiple repos/workflows. ### 4) Generate `name` and `description` from `package.json` - Read `name` and `description` from repository `package.json` during generation. - Write them into `manifest.name` and `manifest.description`. - Fallback behavior (backward compatibility): if either field is absent/empty in `package.json`, preserve current manifest value and emit a warning. ### 5) Keep current generated fields intact - Do not change existing behavior for `homepage_url` and `short_name` generation. ## Implementation notes - Backward compatibility is required: if new metadata exports are missing, keep current behavior and emit actionable warnings. - Add strict validation in CI so generated sections are not manually edited. - Ensure output format is stable to avoid noisy diffs. ## Acceptance criteria - [ ] `manifest.commands` is generated from code metadata (not handwritten JSON). - [ ] `manifest["ubiquity:listeners"]` is generated from code metadata (not handwritten JSON). - [ ] `manifest.skipBotEvents` is generated from a single explicit code source. - [ ] `manifest.name` is generated from `package.json` (or preserved with warning if missing). - [ ] `manifest.description` is generated from `package.json` (or preserved with warning if missing). - [ ] Existing `homepage_url` and `short_name` automation remains unchanged. - [ ] Plugins without new metadata exports continue to build (with clear warnings). - [ ] Tests are added for generation and fallback paths. ## Out of scope - Dist-branch publishing mechanics (tracked in ubiquity-os/ubiquity-os-kernel#320). Cool to see it always recommends at least one person but it is very much not relevant. 

Whats the timeline looking like to populate the database by scraping the existing closed issues and their assignees @sshivaditya2019? 

### repo/org/global Context Matching

I think we should optimize our logic. Tasks that may look similar but posted in two different repositories may in reality be quite different. Normally I would prefer to matchmake against those who completed similar tasks within the same repository, but we can "fallback" to org context (try to matchmake against any repository's task in the org) and then a final "fallback" to global context. 

Perhaps the simplest way to calculate this could be to subtract relevance "points"

Example:
```
0% adjustment: Same repository matching percentage 
-25% adjustment: Same organization
-50%: Global
```

Meaning for an identical task posted in three different locations:
```
same repo = 100% match
same org, different repo = 75% match
different org = 50% match
```

Just an idea but open to discussing to make this more accurate and simple to implement. 

### Recent Code Changes Fallback

Another idea to always try and match somebody is to check how much of the codebase was authored by whom. If nobody hits a relevance of greater than 25% we can fallback to assigning whoever wrote most of the code in the repository. Surely we can find the stats somewhere. 

### Future Considerations

Because we want the system to always be assigning the right contributor at the right time in the future, we should consider the output of the `/start` command as well, with all its checks. If UbiquityOS is able to run `/start` on behalf of others this can solve most of the problems I can think of. 

Specifically, imagine the scenario where the same top contributor is always recommended to work on the newly posted tasks. [^05^] [^04^] [^03^] [^01^] With a concurrent task limit of 2, they will quickly be saturated with work. We should be able to detect this and fallback/recommend/assign the next best.

Issue #1: Custom Notifications Viewer

Description:
- I did some research in the past with custom notifications viewer. https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/pull/126
- Original specification here https://github.com/ubiquity/work.ubq.fi/issues/117

Fork work.ubq.fi because it has a lot of good qualities for list viewing, progressive web app features, styling etc. Tear out all the proposal/task related viewing logic, and focus only on notification viewing so that the code is simpler. 

## Custom Notifications Viewer

As activity continues to pick up and my notifications become slower to get through, it would be useful to make a simple ui that allows for more intelligent notification filtering. 

### Prioritization Sorting Algorithm

- We need to detect the priority level of the task the notification is associated with.
   - If the notification is not associated with a task, consider not showing it on this view at all. 
   - If the notification is a pull request, it must be linked to a task with a priority label.
- Reverse chronological order, meaning that neglected/old notifications should appear higher than new ones. 
   - The reason for this is that active conversations will continue to produce more notifications, which can easily cause the reviewer to check it multiple times in a sitting (as I try to get to inbox 0 this happens to me, so I intentionally start from older notifications for this reason.)
- Top of displayed list is highest priority, then work your way down to low priority. 

### Blocking Tasks

If it thinks without my input the task is blocked, it's a higher priority notification.
- Linkbacks: if the notification is associated with a task with many linkbacks then it should be considered higher priority, it usually means its blocking other pulls/tasks

Perhaps we could have an AI layer on top one day to summarize and/or reorder notifications from most important to least.

### Remarks
- Always exclude draft pulls.

## Notification Scoring

We should associate each notification with "scores" so that we can quantify where it would render on the page. 
- Time score: the older it is, the higher its score. We can take the current posix timestamp and subtract the timestamp of the notification to achieve this. 
- Linkback score: we can count how many times it was cross-referenced. The more times it was cross-referenced, the higher it should render on the page. We should prioritize those with higher linkbacks. If two notifications have the same amount of linkbacks i.e. 0, then we sort based on the time score only. 

We need to ensure that priority level always has precedence. For example, `priority 2` associated notifications should always appear higher than `priority 1`.

Issue #30: Config Protection

Description:
Not sure if this is fully possible from within the webhook event, but the idea is that only admins or billing managers should be able to modify the config because it affects money flow. 

On commit, check if config was modified. If it is unauthorized, rollback the change by immediately committing the previous version as the UbiquiBot. 

This should make it near impossible for fraud.

Issue #443: Migrate backend to Deno-native + harden Deno Deploy

Description:
Context
- Current backend uses Node-specific server (`@hono/node-server`) and `process.env` while deploying on Deno Deploy. This couples Node APIs to a Deno runtime and increases risk of incompatibilities and subtle failures.
- We already deploy via GitHub Actions OIDC to Deno Deploy (project: `pay-ubq-fi`). Frontend is built to `frontend/dist` and served by `backend/server.ts`.

Goals
- Run fully Deno-native on Deploy (no Node server adapter).
- Keep GitHub Actions deploy unchanged except for necessary tweaks.
- Preserve API behavior and static asset serving.

Scope of Work
- Replace server bootstrap with Deno-native:
  - Swap `@hono/node-server` + `serveStatic` for `Deno.serve` + `hono` fetch handler.
  - Use `Deno.env.get()` for configuration.
  - Serve SPA assets from `./frontend/dist` (index.html fallback).
- Supabase client
  - Import via `npm:@supabase/supabase-js` under Deno.
  - Validate ESM usage works on Deploy.
- Add `/health` endpoint returning 200 with basic info (uptime/version).
- Add `deno.jsonc` (server side) with:
  - `tasks` (dev/start/test)
  - Optional import map for `npm:` spec
  - Lint/fmt config
- CI/CD (pay.ubq.fi/.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
  - Keep OIDC deployctl step; ensure `entrypoint: backend/server.ts` still correct after refactor.
  - Ensure frontend build step remains and artifacts exist.
- CORS:
  - Keep current permissive CORS via `hono/cors` or stricter allowlist; document decision.
- Logging:
  - Ensure console logs appear in Deno Deploy logs; standardize error handling.

Acceptance Criteria
- No usage of `@hono/node-server` or `process.env` in runtime code.
- Server starts with `Deno.serve` and exports `app.fetch` handler.
- `GET /health` returns 200 JSON `{ status: "ok" }`.
- Static assets served from `frontend/dist`, SPA fallback serves `index.html`.
- Supabase calls succeed using `Deno.env.get` variables: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- CI deploy completes via `denoland/deployctl@v1` to project `pay-ubq-fi`.
- Docs updated: .rules and docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md reference Deno-native server and env names.

Non-Goals
- Frontend functional changes.
- Schema or Supabase policy changes.

References
- Server: `backend/server.ts`
- CI: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- Project rules: `.rules`
- Deploy guide: `docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md`

Test Plan
- Local: `deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env backend/server.ts` and open site; verify `/api/permits/record-claim` and `/health`.
- Deploy: confirm Deploy logs, static assets, and API endpoints.

Owner/Timebox
- Est: 0.5–1 day. Assign to backend engineer familiar with Deno/Hono.

If Dollar token USD price >1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to a) Mint 1 Dollar token for 1 USD of collateral in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) b) Sell 1 Dollar token on a secondary market 2. On the contrary, If Dollar token USD price <1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to: a) Buy cheap Dollar token on a secondary market b) Redeem Dollar token for collateral worth 1 USD in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) On early project stage any large swap may affect the Dollar token price greatly and the pool (where the swap occurred) may remain unbalanced for a long time which in turn depegs the Dollar token. Issue #997: Integrate Liquity V1 Stability Pool for LUSD Collateral Yield

Description:

## Problem
Plain LUSD collateral earns 0% yield. Integrate Stability Pool for ~6.28% APR ([Dune data](https://dune.com/liquity/liquity-v1)) to fund governance token buybacks, without disrupting liquidity.

## Solution
Add `StabilityPoolFacet` via diamond proxy. Auto-deposit LUSD to pool on mint; withdraw principal on redeem. Harvest ETH/LQTY yields during redeems for buybacks/compounding (protocol-owned only). Piggyback ops on user txs for gas efficiency.

## Alternatives Considered
- AAVE (~3.24% yield, more complex).
- Leverage/LPs (higher risk).
- V2 migration (future option for multi-collateral).

## Implementation Spec
### ~~Prerequisites~~
- ~~Audit facet (~$10-20K budget).~~
- ~~Integrate `IStabilityPool.sol` (address: 0x66017D22b0f8556afDd19e1e5b5f1cbD89a6C337).~~
- ~~Add 1inch/Uniswap for swaps.~~
- ~~New storage: `totalPrincipalInPool` (uint256), `protocolTreasury` (address).~~

### Facet Functions
- `depositToPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `provideToSP(amount, address(0))`.
- `withdrawFromPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `withdrawFromSP(amount)`.
- `harvestRewards()`: Claim rewards, swap (e.g., 50% to LUSD for compounding, 50% to governance token for buybacks).

### Flows
- **Mint**: Transfer LUSD → Deposit to pool → Mint uUSD → Update `totalPrincipalInPool += amount`.
- **Redeem**: Burn uUSD → Calc principal → Withdraw/transfer principal → Harvest if rewards > threshold (route to treasury) → Update `totalPrincipalInPool -= amount`.

### Over-Collateralization
Value pool as LUSD equivalent (Chainlink oracles for ETH/LQTY). Redemptions: principal only.

### Monitoring/Automation
- Chainlink/Gelato for optional harvests. It would be nice to sell the ETH/LQTY for LUSD and boost holdings as soon as it is rewarded by the stability pool.
- Dune alerts for APR/supply.

## Testing
- Unit: Deposit/withdraw/harvest (Foundry).
- Integration: Mainnet fork; simulate liquidations.
- Edges: Low liquidity, volatility, mass redeems. Gas: <200K extra per tx.

## Deployment
1. Deploy facet.
2. `diamondCut` via multisig.
3. Verify on Etherscan.
4. Phased: Opt-in for new deposits.

## ~~Risks/Mitigations~~
- ~~Yield variability: Fallback to plain LUSD if APR <3%.~~
- ~~Supply crunch: Auto-withdraw if < $10M.~~
- ~~Security: Audit for reentrancy.~~

Issue #291: Add retry mechanism for partially failed virtual card order Description: In the virtual card feature, we have two parts in a single transaction to mint a virtual card. 1. Claim the permit by transferring the permit reward to the treasury wallet 2. If the step-1 is successful, order the virtual card at Reloadly The problem is that the transaction isn't atomic because each step happens in a different system. Step-2 can fail while still leaving the permit amount in the treasury. Why would step-2 fail? There could be one of the many reasons. - virtual card suddenly becoming out of stock - any network error on user side or Reloadly side - user closing browser before the permit transaction confirmation - change in the best picked card, suddenly a better card becomes available or currently picked card becomes unavailable - [RPC-handler](https://github.com/ubiquity/rpc-handler) failing to find rpc for backend to use, or if it finds one but the rpc stops working Currently, the solution to this problem is manual. It is either a manual refund or manual resending of the card order request to `/post-order` with some parameters (productId, tx hash, country). We can improve this by implementing one of the following solutions. - a manual refund can become automatic by issuing a new permit of the same amount - resend the mint request to backend to `/post-order` I am inclined towards resending the mint request. One problem is that `/post-order` needs the transaction hash of the permit transfer to the treasury. Sometimes you will have it, and you can store it in the cookies/local storage. But sometimes you will not have it and you will have to read it either from blockchain or ask the user to manually insert the transaction hash to retry minting. I think you can read it from blockchain by looking into [permit2 events](https://gnosisscan.io/address/0x000000000022d473030f116ddee9f6b43ac78ba3#events) The goal of this issue is to implement a mechanism to resend the mint request or a better solution if you can think of one. Since the best-picked virtual card can change in this duration, a better option is to rename the mint button to "Retry Mint" and let the user click first so that user can see they are ordering a different card now. Please note that the virtual cards feature is present in `beta` branch at the moment. But it can move to development branch anytime. So, keep an eye on that and open a PR accordingly. Issue #349: Add support for gift card with SKU 18732

Description:
We have the feature of minting gift cards for crypto rewards which works this way:
1. `pay.ubq.fi` checks contributor's country
2. If contributor's country is in the [MC allow list 3052024.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492174/MC.allow.list.3052024.xlsx) then offer gift card with SKU 18597
3. Otherwise try to find the best card SKU from [MasterCard International.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492175/MasterCard.International.xlsx)

Reloadly has recently added a new tokenized card SKU:
```
We have a new sku that may be of interest to you: 

SKU: 18732
Name: Mastercard Prepaid USD Debit (Virtual only) US
5 - 1000 USD

Product Description:
Your Virtual Promotional Prepaid Mastercard can be used online, for phone/mail orders, or in stores that accept mobile wallet where Debit Mastercard is accepted. This card must be used within 6 months from the time you receive your link. Please Note: A 2% currency conversion fee will apply if the merchant settles in a currency other than USD

This card works in 130 Countries
```

[SKU_ 18732 - Countries covered (5).xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17493171/SKU_.18732.-.Countries.covered.5.xlsx)

It makes sense to support a new SKU 18732 this way:
1. `pay.ubq.fi` checks contributor's country
2. If contributor's country is in the [MC allow list 3052024.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492174/MC.allow.list.3052024.xlsx) then offer gift card with SKU 18597
3. If contributor's country is in the [SKU_ 18732 - Countries covered (5).xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/17493171/SKU_.18732.-.Countries.covered.5.xlsx) the offer gift card with SKU 18732
4. Otherwise try to find the best card SKU from [MasterCard International.xlsx](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/16492175/MasterCard.International.xlsx)

So as a part of this issue we should make sure that SKU 18732 is supported in these pages:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/9b88dd6ffe04a13650d51a055441696a13047be9/static/index.html (redeem gift card)
- https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/blob/9b88dd6ffe04a13650d51a055441696a13047be9/static/ubiquity-dollar.html (mint gift card for UUSD)

Related [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/259#issuecomment-2268350042).

Issue #48: The command `/ask` fails on large contexts

Description:
```diff
! No answer from OpenAI

<!--
{
  "caller": "issueCommentCreatedCallback"
}
-->
```
_Originally posted by @ubiquity-os-beta[bot] in https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings/issues/67#issuecomment-2577541987_


## What happened

The `/ask` command failed to run, due to a context being too large, thus failing with
```json
{
       "res": {
         "error": {
           "message": "Provider returned error",
           "code": 400,
           "metadata": {
             "raw": "{\n  \"error\": {\n    \"message\": \"This model's maximum context length has been exceeded. Please reduce the length of the messages.\",\n    \"type\": \"invalid_request_error\",\n    \"param\": \"messages\",\n    \"code\": \"context_length_exceeded\"\n  }\n}",
             "provider_name": "OpenAI"
           }
         },
         "user_id": "user_2njZil2BmAzm3iDZvVsx69KWg4A"
       },
       "caller": "Completions.createCompletion"
     }
```

Multiple problems here:

- it should use `postComment` so we get the run url and the proper error stack
- there should not be two comments for the failure
- the context should be truncated in some way to allow `/ask` to run properly

## What was expected

`/ask` should truncate the context so it runs properly and still gives an accurate answer.

## How to reproduce

The easiest would probably to run `/ask` against the aforementioned issue, or create an issue with a very long content.
